title.name: Oathbound
title.tagline: Talking matters as much as fighting.

sleep._doc: Keeping hours (Tessera UTSSleep): a sleeper only hears, hearRadius x hearMul; a hit on a sleeper does x hitMul and wakes it; woken, it stays up wakeFor seconds; at the end of their night sleepers get up within staggerUp seconds of each other (not a crowd in one doorway). wokenBarks: what a sleeper mumbles when you wake it to talk.
wokenBarks: Hrm. Do you know what hour it is?

sneak._doc: The Thief crouched (Space, tag Sneaking): foes hear it only within hearRadius x hearMul. Its speed: classes.thief.sneak.speed.

mood._doc: The world's hidden mood (Loom). Peace raises it, killing those who could talk lowers it (tuning moodKill/moodPeace/moodBetray/moodQuest). Bands: thresholds low to high, band 0 in the middle; the game shows the band at dawn / dusk.

moodLife._doc: How many of each ambient kind (x its count) per mood band, from -3 (darkest) to +3 (brightest).

moodDressing._doc: How many of each dressing kind (world3d.dressing) per mood band, -3 (darkest) to +3 (brightest).

languages._doc: Who can talk to whom. Each creature 'speaks' one; each class knows some (classes.<id>.languages, '*' = all). The Scholar speaks them all. Slimes speak none.

stats._doc: Tessera stats and damage rules. A string value names a tuning number. Pools: max = flat stat + base + sum(stat x per); regen per second after regenDelay.

world3d._doc: Unreal-only presentation settings. Gameplay numbers stay in pixels (shared with the HTML prototype); unitsPerPx converts them to Unreal units.

camera._doc: mode 'topdown': fixed 3/4 view, north up (like the HTML map), mouse wheel zooms, the cursor aims. mode 'third': the old over-the-shoulder camera.

abilityPicker._doc: Shift + mouse wheel opens it; the world runs at timeScale while you choose.

dressing._doc: Tessera ATSDressing: small props laid over the world at the game's spots (road, walls = house fronts, sunny = open ground in the village). moodDressing says how many.

ambientLife._doc: Tessera's ambient life (ATSAmbientLife): harmless, can't be fought, flees or vanishes near the hero. Areas from the map: grass, village, road, wild. Counts are at weight 1; moodLife re-weights them.

statusTints._doc: Characters (and ambient animals) tinted while they carry a tag (the first listed wins). Sneaking: the Thief's shadow cloak while crouched.

assets._doc: Assets Tessera loads by name. '/...' = object path; otherwise a Starter Content material name (RPGAssets::StarterMat).

deathGhost._doc: A fallen foe's ghost rises, wiggles and fades (ARPGGhost). Sizes in uu, times in s.

text._doc: Overrides for words Tessera shows (defaults are generic English).
text.bagFull: Bag is full — salvage something (I, Shift+Click)
text.progressLost: There are no saves yet: your current progress will be lost.
text.pickerHint: scroll to change   ·   release Shift or click to cast at the cursor   ·   RMB to cancel

looks2d._doc: Look tests. 'mesh3d' = mannequins + Starter Content. 'hd2d' = pixel-art sprite cards standing in the lit 3D world with pixel textures (Octopath style). 'flat2d' = orthographic top-down pixel map with flat sprites. Override per run with -RPGLook=hd2d|flat2d. Art: tools/pixelart, imported by unreal/Tools/import_pixel.py.

arrows._doc: Arrows fly a parabola: peak height above the straight line = distance x heightPerDistance (uu), clamped.

dayNight._doc: The sun moves from startHour; secondsPerHour of real time per game hour (30 = afternoon to night in ~3.5 min). -RPGHour=21 starts at that hour; -RPGSun= freezes the sun.

fog._doc: Height + volumetric fog, thickening toward night.

nightVision._doc: Deep night: beyond heroSight (uu) and the reach of fires / torches (lightReach x their light radius) the world falls to near black; foes there leave the minimap and lose their labels.

mounts._doc: Where weapon kits attach: a bone plus an offset in that bone's space. Weapon parts are authored with +Z pointing out of the fist.
mounts._measured: -RPGProbe, idle pose: hand_r +Z points forward, hand_l +X points down, lowerarm_l +Z points out to the left

nightLight._doc: A faint white-blue glow that rises with nightfall

knight.name: Knight
knight.tagline: The wall. Takes the most punishment and holds the line.
knight.weapons: One-handed sword + shield, or a two-handed longsword.
knight.defense: Heaviest armor. Blocks with the shield; a perfect block staggers the attacker.

dialogue.desc: Swear oaths, invoke rank, challenge foes to an honor duel.

mage.name: Mage
mage.title: mage
mage.tagline: Glass cannon who fights at range and shields only when he chooses.
mage.defense: Hold right click for an arcane barrier all around you: nothing can get inside it, and anything that reaches you through it (arrows, spells) does 80% less damage. It drains stamina while held.

dialogue.desc: Compel NPCs to agree. It works, but they may resent it later.

thief.name: Thief
thief.title: stranger
thief.tagline: Fragile but fast. Avoids damage instead of absorbing it.
thief.weapons: Daggers (backstab x2) and a bow with unlimited arrows.
thief.defense: No shield. The fastest, cheapest dodge rolls in the game.

dialogue.desc: Threaten and extort. Frightened people comply... for now.

scholar.name: Scholar
scholar.title: scholar
scholar.tagline: Master negotiator. Weakest in a fight, strongest in a conversation.
scholar.defense: Lowest armor. Light shield block and self-healing (Mend).

dialogue.desc: Can talk down almost anyone — for a price, or a promise.

sword_shield.name: Sword & Shield
sword_shield.hint: LMB 3-hit combo · hold RMB to block (raise it just before a hit = perfect block; drains stamina)

longsword.name: Longsword
longsword.hint: LMB slow, wide, heavy 2-hit combo · no block

staff.name: Staff
staff.hint: LMB arcane bolt (free, hold to keep firing) · hold RMB for a barrier no foe can enter (-80% damage, drains stamina)

daggers_bow.name: Daggers & Bow
daggers_bow.hint: LMB fast 4-hit daggers (hit from behind = backstab x2) · hold RMB to draw bow, release to fire

dagger_shield.name: Dagger & Shield
dagger_shield.hint: LMB 3-hit dagger combo · hold RMB to block (light shield: -50%, drains stamina)

shield_bash.name: Shield Bash
shield_bash.desc: Slam your shield forward. Always staggers what it hits. Needs Sword & Shield.

charge.name: Charge
charge.desc: Charge toward the cursor, invulnerable, hitting everything in your path.

cleave.name: Cleave
cleave.desc: A full spin that hits and knocks back everything around you.

fireball.name: Fireball
fireball.desc: Hurl a fireball toward the cursor.

frost_nova.name: Frost Nova
frost_nova.desc: A sphere of frost bursts out around you. Everything caught in it, foe, villager or bird, freezes solid for 3s.

blink.name: Blink
blink.desc: Teleport toward the cursor (can't pass walls or water).

chain_lightning.name: Chain Lightning
chain_lightning.desc: Strike the enemy nearest the cursor; arcs to 3 more nearby, weaker each jump.

volley.name: Volley
volley.desc: Loose three arrows in a fan.

smoke_bomb.name: Smoke Bomb
smoke_bomb.desc: Vanish for 3s. Foes caught in the blast are staggered; others nearby lose track of you — perfect for a backstab. Attacking reveals you.

shadow_dash.name: Shadow Dash
shadow_dash.desc: Invulnerable dash toward the cursor, striking everything in the path.

poison_blade.name: Poison Blade
poison_blade.desc: For 8s, dagger hits poison: damage every 0.5s for 3s.

ward.name: Ward
ward.desc: A ward that absorbs ~40 damage for 10 seconds.

silver_words.name: Silver Words
silver_words.desc: Daze a thinking enemy for 3s. Some will stop and talk — mid-fight. Beasts and the dead don't listen.

insight.name: Insight
insight.desc: Study an enemy: it takes +25% damage for 8s and its next move is revealed.

skeleton_watcher._doc: A variant of the archer ('base'). Hand-written: wants its grave marked.
skeleton_watcher.name: Grave-Watcher

skeleton_captain._doc: Leads the Bonewardens band; wants his lost signet. Robbed of his badge, his band drifts apart.
skeleton_captain.name: Captain Ossric
skeleton_captain.struckBark: You struck the Bonewardens! They raise their bows!

skeleton_band.name: Boneward
skeleton_band.struckBark: You struck the Bonewardens! They raise their bows!

prowl._doc: Robbed of its relic (flag relic_stolen) it leaves the mine at night and prowls the village looking for it, until the relic is back on its hay (relic_returned), it is paid off (relic_paid), or it dies. Stops: tiles; when: night / day.

ferryman_coin.name: Ferryman's Coin
ferryman_coin.desc: An old silver coin, cold as a grave. Some of the dead still owe the ferryman.

rank_badge.name: Bonewarden Captain's Badge
rank_badge.desc: A tarnished badge of rank. Without it, who would follow Ossric?

restPlaces._doc: Where foes sleep (enemies.<id>.rest; their hours: sleeps). spots: [tileX, tileY] beds, each one taken by the nearest sleeper; prop: the card drawn at each spot (an ATSInteractable look); entry: walled off, the sleepers go in by this tile; enclosure: [x0, y0, x1, y1] its walls, with a gate (map '+') the Thief can pick (gate: the lock at the entry); fire: a camp fire.

gate.name: The graveyard gate
gate.bark: Locked. Only the dead pass here.

houses._doc: Every cottage's front door (an ATSInteractable on the door the world builder made). use: house_door. lockedBark: anyone but the Thief; pickTime: seconds the Thief takes to open it. sleeperLift: how far above the mattress top a sleeper lies (uu), so it's on the bed, not in it.
houses.pickHint: Locked. (E, then click: pick the lock)

interactables._doc: Things in the world the hero can use (Tessera ATSInteractable): sheet, size (uu tall), aspect, flat, name, color, dialogue, radius, usable, at [tileX, tileY], showIf (a story condition).

graveyard_burrow.name: Churned earth by the wall
graveyard_burrow.bark: Just loose earth. Something has dug here... often.

brute_food.name: Something to Eat
brute_food.desc: The Ruin Brute will trade the relic for real village food. Find some.

objective.text: Bring the Ruin Brute some village food

maren_slimes.name: Bread for a Brute
maren_slimes.desc: Elder Maren will spare a loaf if you cull five slimes that have been raiding the stores.

grave_rites.name: An Unmarked Grave
grave_rites.desc: A skeleton keeps watch over its own forgotten grave, west under the old trees. Read the rites over it and mark it, so it can rest.

objective.text: Read the rites at the unmarked grave

lost_signet.name: The Captain's Signet
lost_signet.desc: The Bonewardens can't stand down until their captain has his signet back. He lost it in the long grass to the south-west.

toll_bridge.name: The Toll Bridge
toll_bridge.desc: The Red Hands bandits hold the south bridge and toll anyone who crosses. Deal with them — however you see fit.

objective.text: Deal with the bandits at the south bridge

lost_relic.name: The Lost Relic
lost_relic.desc: Recover the village relic from the Ruin Brute in the south-east ruins.

slime_cull.name: Slime Trouble
slime_cull.desc: Slimes keep eating Tobin's stock. Cull five of them in the meadow.

npcs._doc: Villagers. sleeps: night | day (Tessera UTSSleep); house: [tileX, tileY], any tile of the cottage they sleep in (they go in by its door, and only the Thief can follow).

toll_bridge.crossBark: Oi! Nobody crosses without paying! Get them!

text.text: (Maren folds her arms) Folk saw you creeping where you shouldn't, {title}. Ashford still needs help... but we're watching you.
Ah, {title}! The children were singing your name this morning. What can Ashford do for you?
...Oh. It's you. Folk are frightened, {title}. They say blood follows you. What do you want?
What do you need, {title}?
A knight! The crown hasn't sent one of yours to Ashford in years. Please — we need help.
A mage... Folk here don't trust spellcraft. But Ashford can't afford to be choosy right now.
Keep your hands where I can see them, stranger. ...Still. You look like someone who gets things done.
A scholar! Gods be thanked — someone who can actually read. You may be exactly who we need.

choices.text: Could you spare some food? Something big and hungry is sitting on the relic.
By my oath, Ashford is under my protection.
(Slip into her thoughts) What are you not telling me?
Before I risk my neck for your bridge, let's talk about my fee.
Does Ashford keep any old records about that bridge?
Is there anything else I can do?

text.text: Bandits — the Red Hands — hold the south bridge and toll every soul who crosses. A knight could end that. However you see fit.
Bandits hold the south bridge. The Red Hands. I suppose you'd know their kind. Clear them off and there's coin in it.
Bandits — the Red Hands — have taken the south bridge and toll anyone who crosses. Our traders can't reach the road. Deal with them... however you must.

choices.text: It shall be done, by my honor.
Coin first, questions never. I'll handle it.
I'll see what can be done.

elder_bridge_progress.text: The bridge is east of here, where the road meets the river. Brask leads them — proud, greedy, and not as stupid as he looks.

elder_sworn.text: Then Ashford is in your debt, {title}. Take this — it isn't much, but it's what we have.

elder_hypno_ok.text: (Her thoughts unspool) ...the relic. A brute carried the Ashford relic into the south ruins, and with the bridge held, no one can go after it... Why did I just tell you that?

elder_hypno_fail.text: Stop that! I can feel you in my head! ...Try it again and you'll find no welcome in Ashford.

elder_extort_ok.text: ...Fine! Double the reward. Just get it done.

elder_extort_fail.text: I won't be extorted in my own village. The reward stands as offered.

elder_charter_ok.text: Records? ...The old charter! The bridge was granted to Ashford by royal decree. Here — if anyone can make use of it, it's you.

elder_charter_fail.text: Records? I'm afraid whatever we had burned with the old hall.

text.text: They say you beat Brask in fair combat and his men simply walked away. A true knight. Ashford won't forget it.
The bandits just... walked away? Glassy-eyed, I heard. I won't ask how. I'm not sure I want to know.
Brask ran like a kicked dog, they say, and left his loot behind. Remind me never to cross you.
Brask... as our town guard? You may be mad. But if it works, Ashford owes you twice over.
You read them the royal charter and they fled? Ha! The pen and the sword, indeed.
They say you talked Brask down in the middle of a sword fight. In the middle of one! Remarkable.
Thirty gold to end it? Cheaper than a funeral. Well bargained.
Gone, just like that. Whatever you said to Brask, it worked.
You paid them? Well... the road is open for you, at least. They're still there for the rest of us.
They let you pass, but they still hold the bridge. It's a start, I suppose.
The Red Hands woke to an empty purse, blamed each other, and scattered by morning. Brask ran too, they say, jumping at shadows. ...I won't ask where the money went.
The bandits are dead. Harsh — but the road is open.
You already know, don't you... The relic. The brute in the south-east ruins has it. Please, bring it home.
There is one more thing. A brute has made its lair in the old ruins to the south-east, and it took our village relic. Bring it back... carefully.

elder_relic_progress.text: The ruins lie to the south-east, past the archers' woods. The brute hits hard — watch its wind-up and roll away.

text.text: You... took it from under the brute's nose? And it's still alive down there. Gods. It will come looking for this, you know. (End of prototype content — thanks for testing!)
The relic! Ashford owes you a great debt. (End of prototype content — thanks for testing!)

elder_rest.text: Sit by the fire a while... You feel fully restored.

text.text: Back for another lesson, {title}? Fifty gold — or another round on your back.
Made up your mind? Fifty gold.
Halt. This bridge belongs to the Red Hands. Toll's fifty gold. ...You've the look of my little brother about you, lad. Doesn't change the price.
Halt. This bridge belongs to the Red Hands now. Toll's fifty gold — or turn around.

choices.text: The people of Ashford can't pay this. Let them through.
I am a knight of the realm. I challenge you to single combat — your men stand aside.
(Reach into his mind) You're tired of this cold bridge, Brask. Send your men home.
(Spin a dagger) I've cut deeper purses than yours, Brask. Walk away while you still can.
Ashford needs guards, and guards get paid — honestly, every week. I can arrange it.
(Unroll the charter) This bridge is Ashford's by royal decree. Tolling it is a hanging offence.
Westmarch still pays 200 gold for your head, Brask. I'd hate for them to learn where you are.
(Draw your weapon) Then we do this the hard way.

text.text: Single combat? With you? Come back when that armour's seen a real fight, pup.
(A tickle behind his eyes; he swats at it like a fly) Cute trick. Come back when you can do it properly.
(He doesn't even blink) Put the knife away, kid. You'll hurt yourself. Come back when you've bled a bit.
Fine words from someone who's never had to back them up. Come back when people know your name.
You? Come back when you've bled a bit.

skeleton_root.text: (A dry voice rattles out of the skull) Living one... you hear me? Few do. Fewer answer.

skel_toll.text: The ferryman. I never paid him, and he never forgets. Ten coins, and I cross the river for good.

choices.text: [Give the ferryman's coin] He'll take this one. It's his own.

skel_riddle.text: Answer my riddle and I'll go. What walks with you all day, yet never touches the ground?

skel_riddle_right.text: (The jaw clacks, delighted) Ha! Three hundred years and nobody got it. I can go now. Mind your shadow, living one.

skel_riddle_wrong.text: (It shakes its skull slowly) No. Think harder, living one.

skel_song.text: Sing me something from the living days. I've forgotten what music sounds like.

choices.text: (Hum an old tavern song, as well as you can)

skel_song_ok.text: (The bones sway, just a little) ...Oh. Oh, I remember now. Thank you. I can go.

skel_song_bad.text: (It covers where its ears used to be) No. No, that's not music. Come back when you can carry a tune.

skel_bye.text: (The bones settle into an easy walk, off toward the river, lighter than before.)

text.text: (The skull turns west) ...It is marked. I felt it, like a name said aloud after a hundred years.
The grave, living one. West, under the old trees. Read the rites over it and mark it.
I keep watch over a grave no one remembers. It's mine. The earth forgot my name, and it won't let me sleep.

choices.text: How can I help you rest?
It's done. Your grave is marked.

watcher_ask.text: West of here, under the old trees, is a mound with no stone. Read the rites over it, the old words in Grave-speech, and set a marker. Then I can go.

watcher_rest.text: ...Aldric. My name was Aldric. (The bones fold gently to the ground, and something pale rises out of them, unhurried.) (A whisper, already far away:) The others dig in under the west wall of the graveyard, where the earth is soft... Go gently among them, scholar.

text.text: The Bonewardens' names, row on row. You know them now.
A row of worn headstones, the same sigil on each: a shield crossed with a bone. The names are cut deep, the dates shallow.

stones_read.text: Halvard. Brenne. Tomas the Younger... and at the end, a blank stone under the sigil, waiting: OSSRIC, CAPTAIN. (He never gave his own men a grave, and he can't lie down in his own until they're released.)

text.text: A small marker stands over the mound now. The ground feels quieter.
A low mound of earth, older than the trees around it. No stone, no name.

grave_rites_read.text: You speak the old words over the mound. Something in the ground lets out a long breath. You set a small marker at its head.

text.text: (The captain's skull snaps toward your hand) ...That ring. Where did you find it?
South-west, warm-blood, in the long grass. My signet. Bring it.
(Bones clatter to attention behind him) Halt, warm-blood. The Bonewardens hold this field. We march at dawn, every dawn, and never leave it.

choices.text: [Give the signet] Is this what you lost?

captain_why.text: My signet. I lost it the day we fell, somewhere south-west in the long grass. A captain can't dismiss his men without his seal.

captain_thanks.text: (He turns the ring in his finger-bones) ...Bonewardens! Stand down. We are relieved. (The band lowers its bows and files away, one by one.)

band_root.text: (The skeleton points a bony finger at its captain) ...Ask him. He gives the orders.

signet_root.text: Something glints in the long grass: a heavy ring, its crest worn almost smooth.

brute_relic_back.text: (It snatches the relic and cradles it like a baby bird) ...Shiny. MINE. (It shuffles back toward its hay, calmer.)

brute_relic_paid.text: (It bites a coin, then another) ...Hrm. Many shiny. Good. (It stops sniffing at you.)

hay_root.text: (The straw still holds the shape of the relic. The brute will be back by daybreak.)

hay_done.text: (You tuck the relic into the straw. Somewhere in the dark, something big stops hunting.)

text.text: (The brute's nostrils flare) SHINY GONE. Small ones took it. ...You. You smell like shiny.
(The brute sniffs the air hard) ...You. Food? You bring FOOD?
(The brute's eyes narrow) Small one speaks Old Tongue? ...Hrm. Shiny is MINE. Go away.

choices.text: [Give back the relic] Here. Your shiny thing.
[Pay 60 gold] For your trouble. Buy yourself something shinier.
What would you take for the shiny thing?
(Reach into its slow, heavy mind) Give me the shiny thing. Then sleep.
There's gold in the old mine. Dig it, carry it to the village, and they'll feed you every day. I'll teach you how.

brute_wants.text: Hungry. ALWAYS hungry. Ruins have rocks, and rocks are bad food. Bring FOOD, village food, and Shiny is yours.

brute_fed.text: (It tears the loaf in two and crams both halves in at once) ...GOOD. Good food. Shiny is yours. Brute sleeps now.

brute_hypno_ok.text: (Its eyes go glassy. It sets the relic down at your feet, sits, and starts humming to itself.)

brute_hypno_fail.text: (It shakes its huge head like a dog shaking off water) NO. Stay OUT of Brute's head!

brute_too_strong.text: (Its mind is a wall of stubborn stone. Your spell slides right off it.) A mind this thick will take more power than you have yet.

brute_trade_ok.text: (It listens, frowning hard... then its face splits into a huge grin) Brute digs. Brute carries. Village feeds Brute. EVERY DAY? ...Brute is SMART now! Here, take Shiny. Brute doesn't need Shiny. Brute has a JOB.

brute_trade_fail.text: (Its brow knots up. Smoke nearly comes out of its ears) ...Too many words. Brute is hungry, not clever.

brute_too_simple.text: (It stares at you blankly) ...Brute does not understand. Talk smaller. (You'll need more experience to teach something like this.)

brute_calm_root.text: (The brute is curled up at the back of the mine, snoring softly. One eye opens.) ...Mm. Brute is full. Go away nicely.

text.text: Hero! Grot digs gold, Grot carries gold, village gives Grot stew. Children wave at Grot now! Grot has a NAME. Tobin gave it.
Hero! Grot digs gold, Grot carries gold, village gives Grot stew. Grot has a NAME now. Tobin gave it.

elder_food_ask.text: Feed the brute? ...Well, better that than bloodshed, I suppose. But food is short; the slimes have been at our stores. Cull five of them in the meadow and I'll spare you a loaf.

elder_food_given.text: Here, fresh this morning. I hope your brute appreciates good baking.

brask_paid.text: Pleasure doing business. Off you go — and mind the planks.

text.text: (He looks at you a long moment) ...Gods, you sound just like him. Fine. You can pass. Just you, mind.
...Fine. You can pass. Just you, mind — and don't make a habit of it.

brask_duel.text: Ha! A proper challenge. Lads — stand back. Nobody touches the knight. Steel, then!

brask_duel_refused.text: I don't duel tin cans. Get them, boys!

brask_yield.text: Enough! Enough... I yield. You fight like a demon, {title}. A deal's a deal — Red Hands, we're done here. Take my sabre. I won't be needing it.

brask_hypno_ok.text: (His eyes glaze over) ...Tired. So tired of this bridge. Lads... pack it up. We're going home.

brask_hypno_fail.text: (He shakes his head violently) Get out of my head, sorcerer! KILL THEM!

brask_scared.text: (He goes pale) ...Keep that blade away from me. It's not worth it. Lads, we're leaving. NOW.

brask_laughs.text: (He laughs) You? Boys, show this one what happens to people who threaten the Red Hands.

brask_recruit.text: Paid work. Honest work... You'd vouch for us? ...Gods help me, I'm tired of sleeping in the mud. Deal. Red Hands — we're going to Ashford.

brask_charter.text: A royal charter? ...Hanging offence. Right. Lads — we were never here.

brask_counter.text: Clever tongue. Fine — thirty gold and we pack up. Final offer.

brask_blackmail.text: ...You wouldn't. (He studies your face.) You would. Fine. Red Hands — we're moving on.

brask_parley.text: (Brask staggers, blinking) ...Words. Fine — talk, before I change my mind.

choices.text: There's no profit in dying on a bridge, Brask. Walk away and keep your men alive.
(Unroll the charter) This bridge is Ashford's by royal decree. Stop now, or hang later.
Westmarch still pays 200 gold for your head. Keep swinging and they'll hear where you died.

brask_truce.text: ...Fine. FINE. Truce. Red Hands — we're done here. Nobody pays us enough for this.

wren_parley.text: (Wren lowers her crossbow, dazed) ...Why are we even fighting for him?

choices.text: You don't have to. Walk away, Wren — and tell me what you know about Brask.

wren_walks.text: (She drops the crossbow) ...Westmarch. 200 gold on his head. He's terrified of it. I'm done here.

text.text: I've told you what I know. Now go.
Still here?
(The crossbowwoman doesn't look up) Talk to the captain, not me.

choices.text: You don't look like you want to be here either.
What's Brask got over you? You could just walk away.
Lower your crossbow and you have my word no harm comes to you.
(Brush against her mind) What do you know about Brask?
Tell me something useful, or you're first.
I could find you honest work in Ashford. What would it take?

wren_opens.text: (She glances at Brask, then lowers her voice) ...He promised us coin. All we got is mud and his temper. You want leverage? Westmarch has a 200-gold bounty on him. He's terrified of it.

wren_scared.text: Alright, alright! Westmarch. There's a 200-gold bounty on him there. Use it — just leave me out of it.

wren_shuts.text: I've nothing to say to you.

text.text: You. I remember everything, you know. Every second you were in my head.
Honest work. Strange feeling. ...Thank you, {title}. The Red Hands won't trouble Ashford again.
(Tobin moves the cash box out of your reach) I know what you are. Thief's prices, then, and I count the change twice. (You have {gold} gold.)
(Tobin keeps one hand on the counter) Prices are up. Roads aren't safe, folk are scared. Coin up front. (You have {gold} gold.)
Good times in Ashford! Everything's a bit cheaper this week, for you especially. (You have {gold} gold.)
Potions, blades, armor! Coin up front, no refunds. (You have {gold} gold.)

tobin_slime_offer.text: Slimes keep oozing into my storehouse and eating the stock. Cull five of them in the meadow and I'll give you a proper blade.

tobin_slime_progress.text: Five slimes. So far you've squashed {quest:slime_cull}.

tobin_slime_done.text: My stock thanks you! Here — as promised.

map.legend: # wall  T tree  H house  ~ water  = bridge  . grass  , path  r ruins floor. Spawn letters are case-insensitive in Unreal: never reuse one in another case.

areas._doc: Small separate maps built off to the side of the main one (Tessera FTSArea), reached through doors (interactables with door). at = top-left in world tiles, clear of the main map and its hills.
